source_text:
Ἠπάτησέ με ὁ τῆς Μαρίας
υἱός. Οὐκ ᾔδειν, ὅτι Θεὸς ἐν ἀνθρωπίνῳ κρύπτεται σώματι. Ἔβλεπον αὐτὸν σῶμα
ἀνθρώπινον περικείμενον, καὶ ἄνθρωπον αὐτὸν νομίσας ψιλὸν, κατ' αὐτοῦ τοὺς
Ἰουδαίους ἐκίνησα· καὶ ἅπερ δι' ἑαυτοῦ μὴ ἐτόλμων διαπράξασθαι, ταῦτα διὰ
Ἰουδαίων ἐνήργησα. Μυ43.484 ρίας συκοφαντίας ἐφεῦρον· πᾶν εἶδος ὕβρεως εἰς
αὐτὸν ἐπενόησα· καλάμῳ καὶ σπόγγῳ αὐτὸν ἐπότισα· ἀκάνθαις τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ
ἐστεφάνωσα· ῥαπίσμασιν αὐτὸν ἠτίμωσα, σταυρῷ διὰ ἥλων προσήλωσα· θανάτῳ
τέλος ὑποβαλὼν, ὡς νικήσας, μετὰ Ἰουδαίων ἑόρταζον.
Θεασάμενος δὲ αὐτὸν ὅτι τῇ τρίτῃ ἡμέρᾳ ἐγήγερται, καθὼς προεῖπον, ὡς
ξίφος κατὰ καρδίας ἀθρόως δεξάμενος κατέπεσον· θεασάμενος δὲ αὐτὸν ὅτι ἐσθίει
καὶ πίνει, πάλιν ἕτερον σταυρὸν κατεσκεύαζον. Ἀλλ' ὡς ταῦτα ἐνεθυμούμην πρὸς
ἑαυτὸν, ὁρῶ αὐτὸν μετὰ δόξης εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνερχόμενον, ὅθεν ἐγὼ μετ' αἰσχύνης
ἐξέπεσον. ∆ιὸ καὶ Ψαλμῳδὸς ἐκ πολλῶν τῶν χρόνων ἐβόα λέγων· Πάντα τὰ ἔθνη,
κροτήσατε χεῖρας· ἀλαλάξατε τῷ Θεῷ ἐν φωνῇ ἀγαλλιάσεως, ὅτι Κύριος ὕψιστος,
βασιλεὺς φοβερὸς, μέγας ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν· καὶ πάλιν· Ἀνέβη ὁ Θεὸς ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ,
Κύριος ἐν φωνῇ σάλπιγγος. Θέλω αὐτὸν καταδιῶξαι, καὶ ὡς μόλιβδος κάτω φέρομαι·
βούλομαι αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι, καὶ ἀοράτως ἐξαγκωνίζομαι. Τί ποιήσω ὁ τάλας;
Πανταχόθεν με περιήλασεν. Ἐξ οὐρανῶν με ὡς λίθον βραχύτατον εἰς γῆν
ἐσφενδόνησε κάτω. Πεσὼν δὲ ἐν τῇ γῇ, ἐν τοῖς ὕδασι κρυβῆναι ἠθέλησα· καὶ εὑρών
με ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Ἰορδάνου ῥείθροις κρυπτόμενον, ὡς δράκοντα, κρατήσας ἐμάστιξε.
Θέλω κἂν τῆς γῆς κρατῆσαι, καὶ πάντες ὡς δεσποτικῆς νομῆς φύλακες, τὴν κατ'
ἐμοῦ φωνὴν βοῶσι· Τοῦ Κυρίου ἡ γῆ καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς, ἡ οἰκουμένη καὶ πάντες
οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐν αὐτῇ. Ἔδειξεν ὁ σεισμὸς, ὅτι τοῦ Κυρίου ἡ γῆ. Ἡ γὰρ γῆ τὸ τοῦ
Κυρίου ὄνομα μὴ φέρουσα ἀκαρτερήτῳ τρόμῳ ἐβράσσετο, διὰ τὴν ἀταξίαν τῶν
αὐτῆς τέκνων μαστιζομένη, καθάπερ στόμα κατὰ τῶν στοιχείων ἀνοίξασα ῥήγματα,
τῆς κρυπτομένης ὀδύνης ἐβόα τὸ μέγεθος· καὶ φείσασθαι τῶν ἡμαρτηκότων, ὡς
μήτηρ ὑπὲρ τέκνων, ἱκέτευε.
Τίς λαλήσει τὰς δυναστείας τοῦ Κυρίου; ἀκουστὰς ποιήσει πάσας τὰς αἰνέσεις
αὐτοῦ; Τοῦ Κυρίου ἡ γῆ καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς. Τὴν γὰρ σάρκα τὴν ἐκ γῆς
πλασθεῖσαν ἥνωσεν ἐν αὐτῷ ὁ Χριστὸς, καὶ ἐκάθισεν ἐν οὐρανοῖς. Ἔρχεται ὁ
διάβολος διὰ πορνείας μολύνειν βουλόμενος.
thought_title: The devil confesses he was tricked and beaten
orientation: The devil continues his first person lament telling how he drove the Jews to kill Christ and how Christ still rose and went up.
pass_a_gloss: The son of Mary deceived me. I did not know that God is hidden in a human body. I was looking at him wrapped with a human body, and having supposed him to be a mere human, I stirred the Jews against him; and what things I did not dare to bring about through myself, these things I worked through the Jews. Slanders without number I invented; every kind of insult against him I devised; with a reed I gave him drink and with a sponge I gave him drink; with thorns I crowned his head; with blows with the hand I dishonored him, to a cross with nails I nailed him; having laid death upon him as an end, as if having conquered, I was feasting together with the Jews. But having beheld that on the third day he was raised, as I had said before, having suddenly received a sword against my heart I fell down; and having beheld that he eats and drinks, again another cross I was preparing. But while I was turning these things over with myself, I see him going up into heaven with glory, from where I with shame fell out. For this reason also the singer of Psalms from many years before was crying out saying: All the nations, clap hands; shout to God with a voice of rejoicing, because the Lord is most high, a fearful king, great over all the earth; and again: God went up with a shout of joy, the Lord with a voice of trumpet. I wish to pursue him, and like lead I am carried down below; I want to seize him, and without being seen I am thrust off by the elbow. What shall I do, wretched that I am? From every side he has encircled me. From the heavens he slung me down to the earth below like a very small stone. And having fallen on the earth, I wanted to be hidden in the waters; and having found me hiding in the streams of the Jordan like a dragon, having seized me he scourged me. I wish even to seize the earth, and all as guards of a master pasture cry the voice against me: Of the Lord is the earth and its fullness, the inhabited world and all those dwelling in it. The earthquake showed that the earth is of the Lord. For the earth not bearing the name of the Lord was shaken with unendurable trembling, being scourged on account of the disorder of its own children, as having opened rents like a mouth against the elements it was crying out the greatness of the hidden pain; and as a mother on behalf of children it was begging him to spare those who had sinned. Who shall tell the mighty acts of the Lord? Who shall make heard all his praises? Of the Lord is the earth and its fullness. For Christ united to himself the flesh formed from earth, and sat down in the heavens. The devil comes wishing to pollute through sexual sin.

pass_b_english: The devil goes on in his lament: “The Son of Mary deceived me. I did not know that God was hidden in a human body. I saw him wrapped in a human body, and I took him for a mere human and stirred the Jews against him. What I did not dare to do by myself, I worked through the Jews. I contrived myriads of false accusations. I devised every kind of insult against him. With a reed I gave him drink, and with a sponge I gave him drink. I crowned his head with thorns. I shamed him with slaps. I nailed him to the cross with nails. In the end I handed him over to death, and as if I had won, I celebrated with the Jews.”

He continues: “When I saw him risen on the third day, as I had said before, I collapsed as if a sword had suddenly pierced my heart. When I saw him eating and drinking, I was preparing another cross for him. But while I was turning this over in my mind, I see him going up in glory into heaven, from which I fell in disgrace.” Therefore the psalmist also cried out long ago, saying, “All you nations, clap your hands; shout to God with a voice of gladness, for the Lord is the Most High, a fearful king, great over all the earth” (Psalm 47:1-2), and again, “God has ascended with a shout, the Lord with the sound of the trumpet” (Psalm 47:5).

Then the devil says again: “I want to chase after him, but I sink like lead. I want to seize him, but I am thrust off invisibly. What am I to do in my misery? From every side he has encircled me. From heaven he slung me down to earth like a tiny stone. When I fell to the earth, I wanted to hide in the waters. He found me hiding in the streams of the Jordan like a dragon, seized me, and scourged me. If I try even to hold on to the earth, all its keepers, like guardians of a master’s flock, shout the cry against me, ‘The earth is the Lord’s and all that fills it, the world and all who live in it’ (Psalm 24:1).”

The earthquake proved that the earth is the Lord’s. The earth could not bear the Lord’s name and shook with uncontrollable trembling. It was scourged for the disorder of its children. It opened up cracks against the elements like a mouth and cried out the greatness of its hidden pain. Like a mother for her children, it begged him to spare those who had sinned.

“Who will tell of the mighty acts of the Lord? Who will make all his praises heard?” (Psalm 106:2) The earth is the Lord’s and all that fills it. For Christ united to himself the flesh formed from the earth, and he sat down in the heavens. Now the devil comes, wanting to defile it through sexual sin.
notes: Printed Μυ43.484 ρίας breaks the word with a page and column mark; read as μυρίας and glossed as without number.

problems.quote: Here Epiphanius says the psalmist cried out many years ago,
problems.source_quote: ∆ιὸ καὶ Ψαλμῳδὸς ἐκ πολλῶν τῶν χρόνων ἐβόα λέγων·
problems.why: Inserts a third-person narrator ('Here Epiphanius says') into Epiphanius's own direct homily and drops 'Therefore' (∆ιὸ).
problems.fix: Therefore the psalmist also cried out long ago, saying,
problems.ruling: Omits ∆ιὸ (Therefore); weakens causal tie before Ψαλμῳδὸς ἐβόα λέγων.

problems.quote: going up into heaven with glory, from the place from which I fell in disgrace.
problems.source_quote: μετὰ δόξης εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνερχόμενον, ὅθεν ἐγὼ μετ' αἰσχύνης ἐξέπεσον.
problems.why: Adding 'from the place' makes it read as if Christ ascends from where the devil fell, rather than into heaven, whence the devil fell.
problems.fix: going up in glory into heaven, from which I fell in disgrace.
problems.ruling: ὅθεν after εἰς οὐρανὸν means heaven; 'from the place' misreads Christ's ascent.

edits.old: going up into heaven with glory, from the place from which I fell in disgrace.
edits.new: going up in glory into heaven, from which I fell in disgrace.

edits.old: Here Epiphanius says the psalmist cried out many years ago,
edits.new: Therefore the psalmist also cried out long ago, saying,

fixed: [speaker] real: removed third-person narrator and restored 'Therefore / also' per source 'Διὸ καὶ Ψαλμῳδὸς ἐκ πολλῶν τῶν χρόνων ἐβόα λέγων'.
[mistranslation] real: fixed antecedent to heaven per source 'εἰς οὐρανὸν ἀνερχόμενον, ὅθεν ἐγὼ...ἐξέπεσον' = heaven from which I fell, not place Christ ascended from.

problems.quote: Epiphanius says the earthquake proved that the earth is the Lord’s.
problems.source_quote: Ἔδειξεν ὁ σεισμὸς, ὅτι τοῦ Κυρίου ἡ γῆ.
problems.why: Epiphanius is the preacher speaking directly; adding "Epiphanius says" shifts the homily into third-person summary by an outside narrator.
problems.fix: The earthquake proved that the earth is the Lord’s.
problems.ruling: Greek has only Ἔδειξεν ὁ σεισμός; no name—"Epiphanius says" invents third-person narration.

problems.why: Greek προεῖπον is first-person singular ("I said before") or third-person plural ("they foretold"), not third-person singular "he" (Christ).
problems.ruling: προεῖπον is 1sg or 3pl, not 3sg; "he foretold" wrongly assigns Christ, not the Greek form.

edits.old: Epiphanius says the earthquake proved that the earth is the Lord’s.
edits.new: The earthquake proved that the earth is the Lord’s.

fixed: speaker: removed 'Epiphanius says' — source Ἔδειξεν ὁ σεισμὸς has no narrator tag; the preacher speaks directly.
agency: changed 'he had foretold' to 'I had said before' — source καθὼς προεῖπον is 1sg/3pl, never 3sg προεῖπε, so 'he' misstates it; devil as speaker gives 'I'.
